text: For skin disinfection (after cleaning off soiled material): alcohol; iodine-based products (brown colored, e.g. Betadine); and various commercial wound sprays (e.g. for FMD lesions) combining a disinfectant dye (Methylene Blue or Gentian Violet) with an antibiotic (mostly from the Tetracycline family) — the spray form lets farmers treat without handling the animal directly. For premises: always clean before disinfecting, since organic matter and dust sharply reduce disinfectant efficacy; dilute in water following the manufacturer's instructions, and handle concentrated disinfectant with caution. For drinking water: since water is the largest-volume nutrient and is commonly contaminated by animal feces, disinfecting water pumped from a pond, river, or unprotected tank is important to prevent contamination (including H5N1 from wild birds/ducks) — routine treatment with Chloramine is good practice.
